subject: geography
title: Scale, projections, and map choices
objective: Explain how scale and projection shape what a map shows.

lesson.opening: A map is a set of choices. Scale sets how much ground a distance covers, and projection decides how a curved Earth is flattened.

sections.heading: Scale
sections.body: A large-scale map shows a small area in detail, such as a city plan. A small-scale map shows a large area with less detail, such as a world map. The fraction is the map distance divided by the ground distance.

sections.heading: Projection
sections.body: Flattening a sphere always distorts something: area, shape, distance, or direction. Mercator preserves direction but exaggerates high-latitude area; equal-area projections preserve size at the cost of shape.

sections.heading: Choosing a map
sections.body: The right map depends on the question. Navigation favors direction; comparing countries favors equal area; a city walk favors large scale.
